About

A versatile communications profile — built across digital strategy, content creation, and high-stakes campaigns.

I'm a Brussels-based communications professional working across digital strategy, content creation, and media relations. I currently serve at the European Parliament's DG COMM (Directorate-General for Communication), where I facilitate high-profile media broadcasts and promote the Parliament's audiovisual infrastructure to international media actors and MEPs.

With an MA in Political Communication from Cardiff University and an Erasmus at KU Leuven, my experience spans institutional communication, public affairs consultancy, digital and social media strategy, and full campaign management — translating complex messages into clear, engaging communication for diverse audiences.

ALDE Party — Rebuilding Digital Engagement

Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe Social Media Trainee · 1 year
274 content pieces · 1,000+ followers per platform · 20K top video

Challenge

I joined ALDE following a difficult European election cycle in which the party's digital presence had struggled to connect with younger audiences. Content strategy relied heavily on traditional political formats — static graphics, long-form posts, formal tone — resulting in limited reach, weak engagement, and an underdeveloped presence on emerging platforms compared to other European political families.

Approach

I combined analytical research with creative implementation: benchmarking successful practices across the European political landscape, then redesigning the content strategy around a platform-native logic. The core strategic shift was moving towards short-form vertical video, faster reactions to political developments, trend-led content, and a more dynamic and accessible tone tailored to each platform's audience behaviour. I also produced content in collaboration with high-profile figures, including European Commissioners and national ministers.

Result

Over the year I produced 274 pieces of content and grew the party's Instagram and TikTok followings by more than 1,000 each, relaunching the TikTok presence and hitting its full annual growth target within the first quarter. My most-viewed video reached 20,000 views. The role sharpened my ability to combine data-driven decision-making with creative storytelling and deliver timely content in a fast-paced political environment.

02

Political Intelligence — EU Public Affairs Consultancy

Political Intelligence · Brussels EU Public Policy Communications Intern · 6 months
Clients across energy · agriculture · digital · mobility · sustainability
Public Affairs
+
Challenge

Public affairs consultancy demands rapid adaptation across entirely different policy environments, client agendas, and audiences — often simultaneously. Managing full strategic portfolios meant owning each client's communications cycle end-to-end: monitoring legislative developments, producing strategic analyses, drafting press materials, managing media relations, and advising on stakeholder engagement, all while priorities could shift overnight in response to a vote, a Commission announcement, or a media event.

Approach

I developed structured workflows to manage competing deadlines without losing strategic focus, and maintained close communication with both colleagues and clients to stay ahead of fast-moving political developments. Across sectors including mobility, transport, sustainability, technology, and EU public affairs, I translated complex regulatory developments into clear, audience-specific narratives. A project I am particularly proud of was a digital communications revamp for T4SM, a European organisation representing the taxi sector. Rather than reinforcing institutional messaging, I developed a campaign — The Ones Behind the Wheel — that shifted focus to the people the organisation represents. Through interviews and visual storytelling, it highlighted drivers' experiences to demonstrate T4SM's values of sustainability, innovation, and social responsibility in human terms.

Result

The T4SM campaign humanised the organisation's message, increased social media engagement, and generated reusable content across multiple communication channels. More broadly, the role sharpened my ability to work under genuine pressure while maintaining accuracy and quality — balancing simultaneous client portfolios across different sectors and policy environments within a professional Brussels consultancy.

Coimbra 2024 — Parliamentary Campaign

Iniciativa Liberal · Portuguese General Election Communications Director · January – March 2024
+2,000 votes · 30K top video · +500 & +200 new followers

Challenge

Coimbra has traditionally been dominated by Portugal's two largest parties, with smaller parties competing for what is often the final seat allocated through the D'Hondt system. Winning was a long-shot objective, requiring the campaign to maximise visibility and voter engagement with significantly fewer resources than its competitors. Complicating matters further, a wave of vandalism during the election period destroyed a large share of campaign posters across the district — a public incident that attracted media attention and demanded an immediate, carefully managed response.

Approach

Rather than replicating the traditional formats used by larger parties, I designed a communications strategy built around platform-native video content combining political messaging with local storytelling. One activation I am particularly proud of took place outside Coimbra's football stadium ahead of a decisive promotion match — asking supporters whether, if the country's leadership were their football team, they would change the manager. It generated authentic conversations, highly engaging content, and made political issues accessible in a way that formal campaign formats rarely achieve. When the vandalism crisis hit, I worked alongside campaign leadership to coordinate the response — turning what could have become a damaging setback into a demonstration of the campaign's resilience and professionalism under pressure.

Result

The campaign's digital content consistently outperformed competing materials in reach and engagement — my most-viewed video reached 30,000 views, and over a couple of months I grew the candidate's following by 500 and the local party branch's by 200. Although the campaign did not secure a parliamentary seat, it increased the party's vote total in the district by approximately 2,000 votes compared to the previous election, and established communication formats and practices that could be built upon in future campaigns.
